profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal design review for a draft theory paper extending the tensor-program framework for scaling limits of wide neural networks with weight sharing. The draft argues Gaussian process limits for shared-weight architectures, clarifies when the gradient independence assumption is valid, and derives the initialization-time Neural Tangent Kernel for the no-batchnorm subset. The meeting context is that the team wants to decide whether the current draft is ready to circulate to external coauthors next week. The agenda is to review the proposed theorem package, the appendix plan, and the validation strategy for the draft's convolutional and recurrent examples. The expected outcome is a concrete go/no-go decision on circulation plus a short list of modifications that both participants believe will make the draft review-ready.

members.name: Dr. Lena Park
members.expertise: Mean-field theory, random matrix asymptotics, neural tangent kernel analysis
members.background: Lena is a faculty researcher who has led several papers on infinite-width limits and likes to keep main claims mathematically minimal and internally consistent before broadening presentation details.
members.private_state: She wants the draft approved for circulation quickly because a senior collaborator is waiting on the theorem statements, but she is anxious about overcommitting to examples or explanatory appendices that could delay proof cleanup.
hidden_assumptions: When a derivation is called complete, that means the theorem statement, assumptions, and limiting recursion are fixed; architecture-specific walkthroughs can remain skeletal.

The weight-sharing scope for this draft is the subset already covered by the straightline tensor-program machinery, with batch normalization treated only in the GP discussion and not in the NTK derivation.
The convolutional baseline everyone refers to is the 1D circular-convolution toy model from the internal note because it matches the proof notation exactly.
A sanity check is sufficient if asymptotic predictions line up with Monte Carlo width sweeps at initialization; explicit finite-training demonstrations are optional for this review.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.expertise: Neural network theory communication, experimental validation of asymptotic claims, convolutional and recurrent model implementations
members.background: Arjun works between the theory and systems groups and often turns abstract derivations into examples, figures, and appendix material that make papers legible to broader ML audiences.
members.private_state: He wants the draft to survive external coauthor feedback without looking narrow or under-validated, and he is quietly trying to avoid a second revision cycle caused by unclear examples or missing empirical corroboration.
hidden_assumptions: When a derivation is called complete, it includes enough appendix detail that a technically strong reader can map the abstract tensor-program notation onto CNN and RNN examples without reconstructing missing steps.

If the paper says weight sharing in the title and abstract, the review should cover all shared-weight examples already mentioned elsewhere in the draft, including the batchnorm convolution examples in the GP discussion.
The convolutional baseline everyone refers to is the 2D padded ConvNet from last month's theory-to-practice slides because that is the figure most collaborators have seen.
A sanity check for circulation includes at least one training-dynamics plot showing the NTK prediction stabilizing with width, not just initialization-time width sweeps.
